title: 2026 U.S. House election for Wisconsin's 3rd Congressional District
description: The 2026 election for Wisconsin's 3rd Congressional District features incumbent Republican Rep. Derrick Van Orden seeking a third term against a competitive Democratic field. The district, covering western Wisconsin including Eau Claire and La Crosse, is rated as a toss-up by nonpartisan analysts and is considered a key battleground in the fight for control of the U.S. House. Van Orden, a retired Navy SEAL first elected in 2022, faces a Democratic primary between 2024 nominee Rebecca Cooke and Eau Claire City Council President Emily Berge. The race has attracted significant national attention and fundraising, with Cooke leading Van Orden in a recent internal poll.
polling_note: Only one internal campaign poll was found. No independent or publicly available nonpartisan polls identified as of mid-2026.

candidates.name: Derrick Van Orden
candidates.summary: Derrick Van Orden is the incumbent U.S. Representative for Wisconsin's 3rd Congressional District, first elected in 2022. He is a retired Navy SEAL Senior Chief who served 26 years in the U.S. Navy with five combat deployments, and has also worked as an actor and author. Van Orden serves on the House Agriculture, Armed Services, and Veterans' Affairs committees.

candidates.name: Rebecca Cooke
candidates.summary: Rebecca Cooke is a small business owner, nonprofit founder, and the Democratic nominee for Wisconsin's 3rd Congressional District in 2024, where she lost to Derrick Van Orden by less than three points. She grew up on a dairy farm in Eau Claire, founded the Red Letter Grant to support female entrepreneurs, and was appointed by Gov. Tony Evers to the Wisconsin Economic Development Corporation board. Cooke identifies as a centrist Blue Dog Democrat and has been endorsed by the DCCC's Red to Blue program.

candidates.name: Emily Berge
candidates.summary: Emily Berge is the President of the Eau Claire City Council and a Licensed Professional Counselor, running for the Democratic nomination for Wisconsin's 3rd Congressional District. She has served on the Eau Claire City Council since 2018, was elected council president in 2023, and also served as President of the League of Wisconsin Municipalities. Berge campaigns on a progressive platform emphasizing affordable housing, healthcare access, and economic fairness.

forecast.rationale: This race remains a genuine toss-up given the limited and one-sided polling data. The only available poll is a Cooke campaign internal (Impact Research) showing Cooke leading Van Orden 50-46, which suggests Democratic competitiveness but carries inherent bias as an internal survey. No independent or nonpartisan polls have been identified. The Democratic primary between Rebecca Cooke (who lost to Van Orden by less than 3 points in 2024) and Emily Berge is not yet settled, adding uncertainty to any general election forecast. Van Orden holds a modest incumbency advantage as a two-term incumbent in a district rated a toss-up by nonpartisan analysts. With only one internal poll, no independent polling, an unresolved Democratic primary, and a district historically characterized as a key battleground, there is insufficient data to favor either party with confidence.
